user_query: We are planning a Phase 3 randomised controlled trial of a next-generation proteasome inhibitor in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, targeting patients with 2–3 prior lines of therapy including lenalidomide and a prior PI. The trial will be conducted globally across the US, EU, and Asia-Pacific. We are seeking FDA and EMA label claims and will need NICE and ICER submissions. The mechanism involves weekly IV administration with step-up dosing in Cycle 1. Our TPP focuses on improvement in bone pain and physical functioning, but we also need to capture fatigue and treatment tolerability. Please generate a full COA strategy.
assumptions_made: trial_duration_cycles inferred as Unknown — not specified in input

core_domains expanded to include role function and side effect impact summary per FDA 2024 Multiple Myeloma Core PRO Guidance, supplemented by user-specified bone pain, physical functioning, fatigue, and tolerability
answer:
## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** This Phase 3 proteasome inhibitor trial needs PRO evidence to demonstrate superiority in bone pain relief and physical functioning while capturing tolerability advantages during step-up dosing.

**Key challenge:** Major FDA core domains lack coverage in the current candidate pool, particularly for symptomatic adverse events and side effect impact summary required for tolerability claims.

**Recommended starting point:** EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20 for established regulatory precedent [TI-003] with BFI for targeted fatigue assessment and EQ-5D-5L for HTA requirements.

**Critical gap:** BPI-SF absence despite bone pain being a primary TPP claim, and no validated instruments covering FDA-required symptomatic adverse events domain.

## Table 1: Domain Coverage Comparison

| Concept | Key Stakeholder | Current Trial Candidates | IKEMA [TI-001] | TOURMALINE-MM3 [TI-003] | A.R.R.O.W. [TI-004] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Disease-related bone pain | FDA Core | No instrument found¹ | ❌ Not collected | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: Y | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: Y |
| Physical function | FDA Core | No instrument found¹ | ❌ Not collected | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: Y | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: Y |
| Fatigue | FDA Core | BFI — Change: Y | ❌ Not collected | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: Y | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: Y |
| Symptomatic adverse events | FDA Core | No instrument found¹ | ❌ Not collected | ❌ Not collected | ❌ Not collected |
| Side effect impact summary | FDA Core | No instrument found¹ | ❌ Not collected | ✅ EORTC QLQ-MY20 — Change: Y | ✅ EORTC QLQ-MY20 — Change: Y |
| Role function | FDA Core | No instrument found¹ | ❌ Not collected | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: Y | ✅ EORTC QLQ-C30 — Change: Y |
| EQ-5D (HTA utility) | NICE/ICER | EQ-5D-5L | ✅ EQ-5D-5L — Change: Not reported | ❌ Not collected | ✅ EQ-5D-5L — Change: Y |

¹ Not collected in this trial — no KG record.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IKEMA [TI-001] | NR | carfilzomib | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30 (30), EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20), EQ-5D-5L (6) | NR | 56 | 19-25 |
| TOURMALINE-MM4 [TI-002] | NR | ixazomib | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30 (30), EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20) | NR | 50 | 17-22 |
| TOURMALINE-MM3 [TI-003] | NR | ixazomib | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30 (30), EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20) | NR | 50 | 17-22 |
| A.R.R.O.W. [TI-004] | NR | carfilzomib | Proteasome Inhibitor | CSQ-8 (8), EORTC QLQ-C30 (30), EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20), EQ-5D-5L (6) | NR | 64 | 19-28 |
| ENDEAVOR [TI-005] | NR | carfilzomib | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30 (30), FACT/GOG-NTX (n=?), EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20) | NR | n=? | n=? |
| Current Trial (Proposed) | 2026 | Next-gen PI | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30 (30), EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20), BFI (9), EQ-5D-5L (6) | TBD — expert decision required | 65 | 21-28 |

## Table 3: Instrument Gap Analysis

| Instrument | Content Validity | Psychometric Properties (FDA 3) | MCID Evidence | Regulatory Acceptance | Known Gaps / Risks | Fit for Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EORTC QLQ-C30 | validated in general oncology | NR | 5-10 points for functioning scales (improvement) — 5-10 points for symptom scales (worsening indicates deterioration) | FDA/EMA accepted in MM trials; used in multiple approved MM drugs but rarely resulted in label claims (Fernandes 2021) | Multi-domain instrument requiring multiplicity control for subscale analyses — no single-domain focus for bone pain claims | Conditionally fit — highest regulatory confidence tier |
| EORTC QLQ-MY20 | validated in general oncology | NR | Not specifically established for MM population in Cocks 2007 — Generic cancer MCID from EORTC literature: 10 points for multi-item scales | FDA/EMA accepted when used with QLQ-C30; provides MM-specific context but not standalone evidence for labeling | MM-specific module developed pre-2000 — may not capture current therapeutic landscape adverse events | Conditionally fit — highest regulatory confidence tier |
| BFI | validated in general oncology | NR | BFI total scale: 1.33 points (range 0.99-1.70) — usual fatigue item: 1.51 — worst fatigue item: 1.76 | bfi is accepted by fda and ema as a validated fatigue pro instrument for secondary endpoints in oncology trials | interference subscale contains only 6 items (vs 7 in bpi-sf) — mcid formally established only in brain/cns cancer to date | Likely fit — no relapsed/refractory-specific validation on record |
| EQ-5D-5L | validated in general oncology | NR | Index score: approximately 0.04-0.08 (range across national value sets) | eq-5d-5l is currently the preferred euroqol instrument for fda and ema oncology drug submissions for utility-based hrql assessment | country-specific value sets required - a single universal 5l mcid does not exist | Conditionally fit — highest regulatory confidence tier |

| EQ-5D-5L | Secondary | Yes | — | Health utility index — EQ-VAS | Significant improvement | p<0.01 | NR | A.R.R.O.W. (carfilzomib) | NR |
| FACT/GOG-NTX | Exploratory | Yes | — | Additional Concerns neurotoxicity | Significant improvement | p<0.001 | NR | ENDEAVOR (carfilzomib) | NR |

## Table 5: Language & Translation Readiness

| Instrument | Validated Translations (approx.) | Key Languages Covered | Gap / Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| EORTC QLQ-C30 | Verify via PROQOLID | Global coverage expected | No action needed |
| EORTC QLQ-MY20 | Verify via PROQOLID | Major EU/US/Asia languages | Verify Asia-Pacific coverage |
| BFI | Verify via PROQOLID | English, major EU languages | Commission Asian translations if needed — 6-9 months |
| EQ-5D-5L | Verify via PROQOLID | 200+ languages with value sets | No action needed |

## Key Observations

• **Regulatory positioning precedent:** In 57 KG trial-instrument records, 92% of PRO endpoints were positioned as secondary, 7% exploratory, with no primary PRO endpoints documented [Table 4]. This suggests secondary positioning is the established regulatory expectation for confirmatory MM PRO analyses.

• **Domain coverage gaps:** Table 1 reveals that symptomatic adverse events and disease-related bone pain domains lack coverage despite being FDA core requirements and primary TPP claims respectively. EORTC QLQ-C30 pain subscale provides general pain assessment but lacks bone-specific validation.

• **Comparator sensitivity evidence:** [COMP-003] ixazomib demonstrated significant PRO changes using EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-MY20 in the same RRMM population [TI-003], establishing these instruments' change-detection capability in proteasome inhibitor trials.

• **Item library opportunity:** Three KG trials [TI-001, TI-004, TI-005] used EORTC QLQ-C30 subscales rather than full instruments, suggesting calibrated SOA approaches are feasible for burden reduction from 50+ to ~15-20 targeted items per timepoint.

• **Missing BPI-SF precedent:** Despite bone pain being the primary TPP claim, no KG comparator trials used BPI-SF [Table 1], creating precedent uncertainty. EORTC QLQ-C30 pain subscale was the only bone pain measure with regulatory precedent in PI trials.

• **HTA utility coverage:** Table 2 shows 60% of comparator PI trials included EQ-5D-5L, establishing it as standard practice for NICE/ICER submissions in this indication [COMP-002, COMP-003].

## Comparator Analysis

**carfilzomib (EMA Accepted) [COMP-002]** — proteasome inhibitor mechanism — used EORTC QLQ-C30 (GHS/QoL scale only) — achieved regulatory acceptance for symptom and quality of life claims — supports EORTC QLQ-C30 as the primary PRO instrument for this PI class.

**ixazomib (EMA Accepted) [COMP-003]** — oral proteasome inhibitor — used EORTC QLQ-C30 and EORTC QLQ-MY20 — demonstrated significant PRO improvements in convenience and side effect profiles [TI-003] — provides strongest evidence that this instrument combination can detect meaningful change in RRMM PI trials.

**lenalidomide [COMP-004]** — immunomodulatory combination partner — no PRO instruments documented — highlights that this combination context requires PI-specific PRO differentiation given lenalidomide's established role in patient's prior therapy history.

**bortezomib [COMP-001]** — first-generation proteasome inhibitor comparator — no PRO data available — represents the tolerability benchmark that next-generation PIs aim to improve upon, supporting need for comprehensive side effect measurement.

Based on comparator evidence, EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20 has the strongest signal of change in this indication because [TI-003] demonstrated statistically significant improvements across multiple subscales in the same RRMM population receiving PI therapy.

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument | In Candidate List? | Action Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| NICE | EQ-5D-5L | Yes | Include with England value set (Devlin 2018) |
| ICER | EQ-5D-5L | Yes | Include for cost-utility analysis |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. Whether to add BPI-SF specifically for bone pain labelling claims despite lack of PI trial precedent, or rely on EORTC QLQ-C30 pain subscale with established regulatory acceptance.

2. How to address the symptomatic adverse events domain gap — either through CTCAE-PRO supplementation or acceptance that current candidates provide partial coverage only.

3. Assessment schedule aligned with weekly IV step-up dosing — particularly whether C1 weekly assessments are needed to capture tolerability during dose escalation.

4. Endpoint hierarchy positioning — whether any PRO endpoint achieves secondary confirmatory status or all remain exploratory pending upstream efficacy results.

5. Item library approach feasibility — using targeted EORTC subscales (global health, physical function, fatigue, pain) rather than full 50-item QLQ-C30+MY20 battery to reduce patient burden during weekly assessments.
